result:
Everything's in place. Here's the final summary for Riley.

The 30-minute lesson on objective **O3 — context and memory** is ready at `lessons/0001-context-and-memory.html`. It covers:
- what's actually in the context window for one turn (vs. training, vs. an unread manual)
- what carries forward step-to-step within a session by default
- the fixed token limit and context rot (why more isn't automatically better)
- why nothing survives between sessions unless it's saved
- notes as memory, and retrieval — searching a big source for just the relevant slice

It uses your RAM/disk, cooking, and Python-dictionary analogies throughout, tied back to the makerspace assistant, and ends with a worked example sorting a real booking request into the three buckets (context / note / retrieval). It went through two review passes — one citation got swapped out because it didn't actually support the claim it was backing, and a couple of missing misconception call-outs got added.

A short 5-item quiz (`quizzes/0002.json`) is ready whenever you want to check what stuck — just ask. There's also a one-page cheat sheet at `cheatsheets/context-and-memory.html` with the terms, the three-bucket sort, and the common mix-ups, for whenever you want to look this up again without rereading the whole lesson.

Ask me anything about it in chat — and let me know if 30 minutes was the right length, or if you'd want it shorter/longer next time.
